problem: Learning-based tuners for optimization-based local planners (DWA/TEB) rely on RL trained in simulation, so they suffer a sim-to-real gap and limited scene diversity, and they ignore obstacle semantics. Directly prompting an MLLM for hyperparameters just returns toolkit defaults.
motivation: Service robots such as smart wheelchairs operate in changing, human-centric scenes where fixed planner parameters degrade performance and social acceptance. Human experts tune parameters by judging the scene along a few dimensions, so an MLLM can supply that scene judgment while a small generative model learns the expert's tuning from real-world data. This keeps classical planner safety guarantees and gives an interpretable pipeline.
key_idea: Use an MLLM (one-shot exemplar plus chain-of-thought prompting, with YOLO help) to turn camera frames into a numeric scene-rating matrix, then use a CVAE conditioned on this rating to generate expert-like DWA/TEB hyperparameters online.
insight: Decoupling perception (MLLM) from hyperparameter generation (small CVAE) avoids the MLLM's default-value bias and permits training on a few real expert sequences. The packet-loss ablation shows that dropping the latest two frames gives about 17.9% error for TEB without augmentation versus 9.43% with it, so masking-based robustness matters. The real-world trials show the expert-data-driven approach generalizes to unseen scenes better than sim-trained RL (DADWA).
method: Scene rating via MLLM: the MLLM assesses five dimensions (pedestrian presence, density, movement direction, proximity as foreground; background environmental complexity) and outputs a structured numeric scene-rating matrix, optionally with token logprob confidence.
Induction phase: a rule set plus a one-shot expert reasoning exemplar and a fixed output schema make the MLLM output consistent and parseable.
Deduction phase: chain-of-thought sub-question decomposition improves accuracy and auditability; YOLOv11 assists with human proximity estimation, which MLLMs handle poorly.

CVAE modulator: a Transformer condition encoder over a short history of scene ratings, MLP encoder (training only) and MLP decoder generate 9 min-max normalized hyperparameters (8 planner parameters plus global costmap inflation_radius); loss is KL plus MSE.
Packet-loss robustness: during training, frame features are randomly dropped and masked in attention, so the model tolerates delayed or lost MLLM outputs.
Deployment: dynamic reconfigure in ROS move_base tunes TEB or DWA at 0.5 Hz; normalized outputs allow user-personalized speed ranges; no action chunking or smoothing is used.
New Score metric: combines success rate with normalized time, acceleration, jerk and TTC-based safety rates.

setting.backbone: Qwen-VL-Max (frozen, scene rating; GPT-4o and Kimi also tested) + YOLOv11 + Transformer/MLP CVAE (trained from scratch)
setting.model_size: CVAE is lightweight (<0.5 GB GPU memory to train); MLLM size not specified
setting.training_data: Real-world expert tuning: 53 TEB sequences (44 train/9 val) and 56 DWA sequences (47 train/9 val), images at 0.5 Hz with expert-set hyperparameters
setting.observation: Monocular RGB (RealSense D435i) for the MLLM, plus RS-LiDAR-16 for localization and obstacle detection
setting.action_space: Planner hyperparameters (9-dim) for DWA/TEB, which then output velocity commands
setting.simulator: real world only (Gazebo used only to train the DADWA baseline)
setting.privileged: none (global costmap/localization from LiDAR; preset pedestrians only in test design)

numbers_note: No standard embodied navigation benchmark; evaluation is on custom real-world wheelchair scenarios (Table III) and hyperparameter-error tables (Tables I-II), which have no canonical benchmark name and are not reported as numbers entries.
results: Hyperparameter error stays under 10% with all three MLLMs (GPT-4o best at 3.60% TEB and 3.84% DWA Top-Err). In five real-world scenarios (3 runs each), LE-Nav variants achieve the best or near-best Score and fewer failures than DADWA. For example, in Scenario (e) LE-Nav-TEB scores 0.8238 versus DADWA 0.5600, and in Scenario (a) DADWA fails 3/3 runs. A user study rated LE-Nav above DADWA on all five dimensions.
limitations: MLLM latency (0.5 Hz) and packet loss limit real-time scene understanding, and the smaller MLLM is used for speed; YOLO is needed for proximity.
Small expert dataset (about 50 sequences per planner), only two planners, one platform, few trials per scenario (3 each).
Not always best: in some scenarios human-tuned baselines score higher (e.g. Scenario (b) DWA-progressive 0.7313 vs LE-Nav-TEB 0.6975), and LE-Nav-DWA has 1 failure and Score 0.5345 in Scenario (e).
